question: Should OpenClaw publish a public OpenAPI/Swagger contract for Gateway programmatic access, and should that contract be a static artifact, an authenticated runtime endpoint, or a documented TypeBox/JSON Schema client-generation path?
rationale: The implementation would define a supported external Gateway API surface, including auth, scopes, endpoint visibility, versioning, and upgrade compatibility; automation should not choose that contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design public schema contract first
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers choose the supported schema format, exposure path, versioning model, and security boundary before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to generated static artifact
options.body: Accept a committed or release-attached schema artifact for client generation and avoid adding a runtime schema endpoint for now.

options.title: Document existing protocol path
options.body: Decide that TypeBox/JSON Schema plus Gateway RPC docs are the intended client-generation surface instead of OpenAPI/Swagger.

recommendation.title: Design public schema contract first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers choose the supported schema format, exposure path, versioning model, and security boundary before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current-history owner for the Gateway protocol/schema boundary this request would change.
